title: Private upgrade pause/resume coordinator and transactional migration backstop
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a pause/resume coordinator and a transactional 'backstop' for Redwood Private upgrades so long-running schema migrations and multi-service state transitions can be safely paused, resumed, or fully compensated without violating tenant SLAs or leaving agents in inconsistent states. This ticket delivers the control-plane coordinator, tenant-scoped pause tokens, a minimal compensating transaction runner, and the rollout gating hooks that integrate with LTS channel semantics and existing canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes /pause and /resume endpoints scoped by deployment and tenant-id and requires operator auth via existing RBAC tokens
A tenant-level pause token prevents new write-intense upgrade steps (schema migrations, cache invalidation waves) while allowing read traffic and emergency admin operations
The migration backstop can replay or compensate a failed migration step within a bounded time window and mark migrations as resilient or fatal
Rollout gate integrates with console: when paused, Console shows per-tenant state and provides one-click resume with audit log entry
Automated e2e tests simulate interrupted migrations and demonstrate successful resume or compensating rollback in >= 3 scenarios
Telemetry instruments pause/resume events, duration, impacted tenants, and success/failure of compensating operations
migration_plan: Phase 1 — control-plane API and internal state machine: implement coordinator service that tracks active migration runs, per-tenant pause tokens, and step checkpoints. Phase 2 — lightweight compensator library: provide idempotent compensation primitives for known subsystems (DB schema, KV cache, deployment rollout). Phase 3 — integrate hooks into private-upgrade runner and canary gating so upgrade steps check pause state and publish checkpoints. Phase 4 — progressively enable for small customers in dedicated staging, then limited internal on-prem lab, then customer opt-in beta, then default on LTS-1 channel.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal deployments (staging-lab) using feature-flagged coordinator. Enable tenant opt-in beta for non-critical customers. Use canary cohorts of 5%/25%/100% with automated health checks (latency, token errors, migration step completion) and an automatic halt on failure. LTS channels: apply to private-LTS-1 as a patch only after successful beta and documented compensating actions. Provide a manual operator 'safestop' that blocks further upgrade waves but allows emergency rollbacks.
observability_checks: Compensator success rate and error class breakdown
Console dashboard tile with active paused migrations
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator state transitions (requested, paused, resumed, failed)
Integration test: inject failure mid-migration, assert compensator runs and system reaches consistent state
Chaos test: kill worker nodes during migration, reintroduce and resume
Security test: ensure pause/resume endpoints are RBAC protected and logged
Performance test: measure latency impact of pause checks under 99th token latency budget
known_risks: Compensating transactions may be difficult for some legacy on-prem customers with custom DB extensions
Operator misuse could leave migrations indefinitely paused — need UI guardrails and TTLs
Coordination window may increase upgrade duration; batching thresholds need tuning
Audit log volume spike when many tenants use pause/resume concurrently
